subject: Meteorology
title: Scattering of Light
description: A fast breakdown of Scattering of Light for builders.

hook.text: The sky is blue because air molecules scatter blue light more than red—it's physics, not pigment.

buildup.text: This is called Rayleigh scattering—shorter wavelengths bounce around more when hitting tiny particles.

discovery.text: At sunset, light travels through more atmosphere, scattering away blue and leaving reds and oranges.

twist.text: On Mars the sky is butterscotch by day and blue at sunset—the opposite of Earth, due to dust size.

climax.text: Volcanic eruptions can inject particles that create vivid red sunsets worldwide for months afterward.

punchline.text: Blue skies are just scattered sunlight—nothing more.

quiz.question: What causes the sky to appear blue?
